title: Bucanus: knowledge, assent, appetite — firm trust and personal application of Christ
source_text: XI. Bucano vero Lausannensi Theologiae Professori, fides definitur, Notitia, assensus, & appetitio promissa in verbo gratiae, adeoque salutis propter Christum obtinendae firma fiducia & apprehensio. Vel, Ex mentis notitia & approbatione judicioque speciali, voluntatis sive cordis desiderium & apprehensio, qua Christum crucifixum cum beneficiis suis in verbo & sacramentis oblatum singuli veri fideles nobis ipsis applicamus. Loco 29. quaest. 7.
pass_a_gloss: But for Bucanus, Professor of Theology at Lausanne, faith is defined as Knowledge, assent, and appetite of what is promised in the word of grace, and so a firm trust and apprehension of salvation to be obtained for Christ’s sake. Or, From the mind’s knowledge and approval and special judgment, a desire and apprehension of the will or heart by which we each as true faithful apply to our very selves Christ crucified with His benefits offered in word and sacraments. Place 29, question 7.
pass_b_english: Bucanus (Lausanne): knowledge, assent, and appetite for what grace’s word promises.
Firm trust/apprehension of salvation for Christ’s sake.
Or: mind’s knowledge and approval → heart’s desire and grasp.
True believers each apply crucified Christ and His benefits (word and sacraments) to themselves.

lemmas.latin: Notitia, assensus, & appetitio promissa in verbo gratiae
lemmas.gloss: Knowledge, assent, and appetite of what is promised in the word of grace

lemmas.latin: Christum crucifixum … singuli veri fideles nobis ipsis applicamus
lemmas.gloss: we each as true faithful apply to our very selves Christ crucified

rejected: Bucanus reduces faith to bare notitia without application
